objective:
Implement wave B slice B3 in workflow: one vendored Python validator and one vendored JavaScript validator for the frozen rizzstack.brief/1 and rizzstack.attempt/1 schemas. The approved RED tests are tests/test_wave_b_validators.py at source_rev 735d2acd973b7585ff1be87f3b25cb58b6ef3163; read them first and do not edit them. The approved contract is contracts/wave-bc/B3.contract.json, embedded below; the tests are the authority if the two disagree.

Create exactly two files. validators/python/rizzstack_validators.py is a standard-library-only JSON Schema subset checker for the two frozen schemas: validate_brief(document, *, schema_dir=None) -> list[str] and validate_attempt(document, *, schema_dir=None) -> list[str]. Empty list means valid; each entry is one human-readable path-plus-message problem. Load the schema JSON from schema_dir at call time (default: the repository schemas/ directory) and enforce every keyword the frozen documents use: type, const, enum, required, properties, additionalProperties, items, minItems, maxItems, uniqueItems, minLength, maxLength, pattern, minimum, maximum, allOf and if/then. observability/validate.py is the in-repo precedent for a small stdlib subset checker, but do not hardcode its schema directory: the schema_dir argument is part of the contract and the tests mutate a copy of the schema to prove the verdict follows it. Do not import jsonschema, PyYAML or any third-party module; the tests executed it under python3 -I -S.

validators/js/rizzstack-validators.mjs is a standalone ES module with no imports and no package.json: export validateBrief(document) -> string[] and validateAttempt(document) -> string[]. Because it may not import fs, carry the schema-derived rules inside the module (a generated literal or a hand-written subset that the parity test proves equal). It must reach the same verdict as the Python module and as jsonschema on the shared corpus. Do not add ajv, a package.json, a lockfile, a requirements file, a CI job or a changelog entry. Do not touch any other file: no dispatch client, no schema edit, no bundlebees code.

Leave every change uncommitted in the worktree. Do not commit, amend, tag, push, force-push or open a PR. Do not revert or clean files outside your two-file lease. If a test seems wrong, stop and report rather than editing it. Keep the files free of host names, absolute local paths, tokens and internal endpoints. Report the two test commands' output and git diff --stat.

criteria: AC-001: the Python validator accepts the minimal brief and attempt, refuses a brief missing any of the seven required fields, and refuses a high-tier brief without contract while accepting the same brief with one
AC-002: the JavaScript validator reaches the same accept/refuse verdicts as the Python validator on the minimal documents, every missing required field, and the high-tier contract rule

AC-003: both validators are checked against the frozen schemas: the Python verdict follows an alternate schema_dir, and both match jsonschema on the shared 38-document corpus including every approved example

AC-004: neither validator ships or needs a runtime dependency: no dependency manifest exists under validators/, the Python module imports only the standard library and runs under -I -S, and the JavaScript module contains no import or require

AC-005: the two module interfaces match the contract exactly: one function per schema, a list of string problems returned, empty meaning valid, and the documented schema_dir keyword on the Python side
AC-006: bundlebees and hyvv can vendor the Python file and Orbit and the control plane can vendor the JS file unchanged, with no per-consumer fork or schema copy in this slice
AC-007: the full tests/ suite passes with no new failures beyond the pre-existing environmental set, and no consumer, schema, CI or changelog file is modified

reasons: the two modules become the single cross-repo truth for brief and attempt validation in bundlebees, hyvv, Orbit and the control plane
a validator that is stricter or looser than the frozen schema silently changes what every dispatch client accepts
a dependency added to either module would propagate into four consumers, which is exactly what this slice forbids
risk.blast_radius: bundlebees, hyvv, orbitdesktop and the orbit control plane brief/attempt handling

contract.title: Vendor one Python and one JavaScript validator for the frozen brief and attempt schemas

outcome.summary: Wave B's frozen schemas get exactly two vendored validators and no new runtime dependency: a standard-library Python module that bundlebees and hyvv copy, and a standalone ES module that Orbit and the control plane copy. Both expose one function per schema, return a list of problems (empty means valid), and reach the same verdict as jsonschema reading the frozen schemas on a shared 38-document corpus. The Python module is driven by the schemas directory it is handed; the JavaScript module carries the schema rules inside itself because it may not import anything. No consumer code, no dispatch wiring and no CI job changes in this slice.
observable_behavior: validators/python/rizzstack_validators.py imports only the standard library and runs under python3 -I -S, so it cannot depend on an installed jsonschema
validate_brief returns [] for the minimal brief and for the approved brief examples, and a non-empty list for a brief missing any required field or a high-tier brief without contract
validate_attempt returns [] for the minimal attempt and the approved attempt examples, and a non-empty list for an unknown state or an unknown field
pointing validate_brief at a copied schemas directory whose required list was extended adds the new field to the refusal, proving the schema drives the verdict
validators/js/rizzstack-validators.mjs exports validateBrief and validateAttempt, contains no import or require, and returns the same verdicts as the Python module
both validators agree with jsonschema on all 38 corpus documents (27 constructed cases plus 11 approved examples) and with each other
validators/ ships no package.json, requirements.txt, pyproject.toml or Pipfile, so no consumer acquires a runtime dependency by vendoring it

interfaces.name: validators/python/rizzstack_validators.py
interfaces.notes: stdlib only; validate_brief(document, *, schema_dir=None) -> list[str] and validate_attempt(document, *, schema_dir=None) -> list[str]; empty list means valid; schema_dir defaults to <repo>/schemas and must govern the verdict

interfaces.name: validators/js/rizzstack-validators.mjs
interfaces.notes: standalone ES module, no imports and no package.json; export validateBrief(document) -> string[] and validateAttempt(document) -> string[]; schema rules embedded because the module may not read the files at runtime

interfaces.name: schemas/rizzstack-brief.schema.json
interfaces.notes: read-only source of truth; the B3 validators must follow it, not redefine it

interfaces.name: schemas/rizzstack-attempt.schema.json
interfaces.notes: read-only source of truth; the seven-state enum and success shape are enforced by both validators
